subject: Urgent: Renewal Relief & Custom Credit Request — HeliosSpark
messages:
From: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@heliosspark.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service degradation during renewal window — impact & request

Hi Marissa,

Quick summary: on 2027-04-14 between ~10:40–13:50 PT we saw consistent tail latency spikes across our inference traffic. Spike correlated with a large batch import and resulted in timeouts for ~3% of our ingestion pipeline; downstream retries caused visible customer-facing errors. Our SLO for 99th pct latency is 120ms — observed 99th was ~420ms for a ~3-hour window.

We're mid-renewal with HeliosSpark and this incident materially impacted our partner demo last night. We need a proposed remediation/credit and assurance for the renewal committee. Can Redwood provide: (1) a written incident summary, (2) a compensatory credit proposal (we're evaluating either a free month or equivalent $ credit), and (3) any short-term mitigations you can apply to prevent recurrence before renewal?

I've attached our logs and a short customer-impact write-up. Please loop in anyone necessary — the renewal decision is sensitive to how we handle remediation.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramirez
Head of Integrations, HeliosSpark
Alicia Ramirez | HeliosSpark, Inc.
Attachment: heliosspark_incident_report_2027-04-14.pdf (PDF, 380 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@heliosspark.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation during renewal window — impact & request

Hi Alicia — thank you for the clear summary and the attachments. I’m really sorry HeliosSpark hit this at such a bad time. We’ve already initiated an Ops runbook and are collecting full telemetry; initial findings point to an unexpected KV-cache eviction pattern combined with a large concurrent batch that degraded tail latency.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Ops (Karthik / infra) will circulate a root-cause summary within 24 hours.
- I’ll prepare a commercial proposal for remediation credits and short-term concessions for the renewal committee.
- We’ll set up a hands-on call with your SREs today to walk through mitigations.

Provisional options I expect to propose (subject to exec approval):
1) One month of service credit applied to the next billing period + a one-time operational review (no cost).
2) If HeliosSpark prefers an economic offset, a tiered credit equal to 20% of April invoice pro-rated across next two invoices.

If you have a preference between (1) or (2), or a target number that would satisfy the renewal committee, let me know — that’ll help expedite approvals.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation during renewal window — impact & request

Marissa / Jonas — quick ops note: we pulled the traces and confirmed the KV-cache eviction cascade; root cause appears to be an unanticipated batch size from HeliosSpark's backfill that deleted hot prefixes and forced cold starts across GPUs. We've implemented a short-term guardrail that rejects imports above threshold and patched the allocator to better preserve hot caches during bulk imports. Telemetry since ~13:10 shows latency returning to expected distribution.

On credits — from an Ops/CS standpoint I recommend a modest commercial concession tied to renewal: (A) one month credit OR (B) a $30k credit split across next two invoices, plus a commitment to a free performance tuning session. HeliosSpark's ARR with Redwood is moderate (current MRR ~$85k), so (A) is a reasonable signal of partnership while minimizing precedent risk.

I’ve attached a quick billing calc for the alternatives.
Attachment: heliosspark_billing_offset_calc_2027-04-15.xlsx

Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec approval requested — HeliosSpark concession options

Jonas — per the thread below, HeliosSpark is requesting compensation tied to the April incident; they’re in active renewal review and timing is tight. Customer preference unknown but they indicated the renewal committee is influenced by the size of the remediation.

Options we’d like exec sign-off to offer (pick one):
- Option 1 (Conservative): One free month applied to May 2027 invoice + free performance tuning session (no revenue hit beyond that). Estimated revenue impact: ~ $85k MRR pro-rated -> ~ $65k realized value for a month.
- Option 2 (Caped credit): $30,000 one-time credit split across next two invoices + performance tuning session. Lower immediate revenue hit; still demonstrable goodwill.
- Option 3 (Escalation-level): If retention risk is high and legal is comfortable, authorize up to $50,000 one-time concession (needs VP sign-off).

We recommend Option 2 by default — balances customer retention and precedent. Requesting fast approval so I can get a signed addendum on the renewal. Please reply with the option you approve and any guardrails (e.g., no precedent beyond 1-year term, attach SLA addendum).

—Marissa
